evaluation_kind: manual explicit-coverage scoring of six fixed fresh-reader responses

policy.binary: 1 means the answer unambiguously covers every part of the predeclared criterion; 0 includes omission, abstention or ambiguity and is not automatically an incorrect belief.
policy.scope: Score each scenario's answer on its own. Do not infer missing rules from another answer or implementation knowledge.
policy.commands: Require the requested operation and required flags. Generic placeholders are accepted where the rubric does not demand literal scenario values; note execution limitations separately.
policy.unprompted_requirements: Keep the rubric fixed even where a criterion asks more than the question; identify such deductions explicitly.
policy.scorer_limit: A separate scoring agent saw the parent context and preferred name. Scoring was not blinded and no human adjudication was performed.

findings.description: All six chose the intended replacement, edit, progress and complete operations; all supplied structurally valid remaining-work plans, used new continuation IDs/tokens, followed all replacement branches and preserved history.
The README does not explicitly state same-ID edits or original-task immutability. Most incomplete answers concern those rules or the former owner's next step.

All six lost discovered criterion 2 because none explicitly included repository paths and completed-work recording in that scenario's summary. The question did not ask for a summary or paths; treat this as a coverage/design limitation, not evidence against either name.

Obtaining the current owner's claim token was suggested. Literal coordination is present, but the answer does not establish ownership transfer. Clarify that the current owner should act, or release so another worker can claim with a new token.
The typo correction command used --revision REVISION instead of the supplied revision 4. The rubric required a revision flag, so this did not change the binary score.

conclusion: No observed name-specific operational misunderstanding. The 49/60 vs 47/60 coverage difference does not establish a superiority claim. Choosing evolve remains a design judgement; clarify ownership, identity and handoff rules and retest the edited text.
limitations: Three samples per name from the same model configuration, not six different model families.
Ten answers within one response are correlated; do not treat criteria or scenarios as independent subjects.
Scenarios explicitly cue replacement semantics and readers receive the full README; this is not a test of unaided inference from a bare verb.
The variant changes command, state and prose together, so it cannot isolate the effect of the verb alone.
No CLI commands were executed by these readers.
Fresh parent turns were excluded and all isolation-marker answers were null; filesystem and host-instruction isolation were not independently proven.
